full_judgment:
25. Now let us see what is the law regarding the burden of proof Section 101 of the Evidence Act lays down the provision of the Burden of Proof which runs thus: 

 When a person is bound to prove the existence of any fact, it is said that the burden of proof Iies on that person." 

 26. The burden of proof lies on the party who substantially asserts the affirmative of the issue and not upon the party who denies it. It is reasonable and just that the suitor, who relies upon the existence of a fact, should be called upon to prove his own case. The party on whom the onus of proof lies must, in order to succeed, establish his case and he cannot on failure to do so, take advantage of the weakness of his adversary's case. He must succeed by the strength of his own right and clearness of his own proof. Here in this case both the plaintiffs and the contesting defendant have made out two distinct cases which each of them has to prove his respective part. 

 31. In the instant case, the proof of pattan taken by Gogan Chandra Sutradhar is a very important factor upon which the whole case of the contesting defendant relies. Without the proof of this point, the entire case of contesting defendant falls down. If the title of Gogan Chandra Sutradhar is not proved, the title of the defendant No.1, Ayesha Khatun, by virtue of Kabala No. 2373 dated 15-5-1959 will also not pass and which will prove the defendant No.1 or her heirs, who are petitioners Nos.1(a) to 1(e), as trespassers in the 'Kha' scheduled land.
